summary: Honduras is shown at the grain of the IMF’s Government Finance Statistics: the central government and its social security funds, 16 lines of taxes and social contributions for 2020, in HNL. The largest line is value added tax (32%), then excises (14%) and corporate income tax (13%). Taxes on goods and services (VAT, sales taxes, excises, vehicle and similar taxes) make 49% of the total and income taxes 23%; social contributions are 22%. The folio records what each line raised; it does not describe the country’s tax laws, rates or the names of its individual taxes.
structureNote: This folio is built from one source, the IMF’s Government Finance Statistics (Statement of Operations), for 2020: central government including social security funds (S1321). Sub-national governments are not drawn: the IMF series does not report taxes for them in this year. Imputed social contributions (HNL 29.1 million) are not cash taxes and are left out. Lines below 0.15% of the total are folded into one “small lines” core per level; lines that the IMF reports only as a parent are drawn as the parent. Rates, legal bases and the names of the individual taxes are not recorded. The IMF labels the series 2020; where the country’s fiscal year is not the calendar year, this is the fiscal year the IMF assigns to 2020. The figures are the IMF’s and have not been compared with the country’s own statistics. There is no OECD level layer for this country in the atlas.

denominators.calculation: Sum of the 16 lines drawn (HNL million). The IMF reports 110,544.308 million for the sector; the lines drawn differ from it by 0 million (rounding between levels of the classification).
denominators.caveat: The IMF flags the figures for this year as actual. The IMF labels the series 2020; where the country’s fiscal year is not the calendar year, this is the fiscal year the IMF assigns to 2020.
